doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Spike Lee, the Bass Choir and Hinton's recording work
summary: Williams raises Spike Lee, and Hinton recalls him conducting the young bass player's choir while Richard Davis, Ron Carter and he made the money.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Who is that young man, Spike Lee? Son of a bass player in Chicago? Mo Betta Blues.
Spike Lee. Really. I worked with him he’s one of the most magnificent men. A true flower child.
Isn’t he, really. He was part of the choir.

He was a conductor in the Bass Choir, in the young bass player’s choir. He was a conductor. And then he didn’t have anybody, and didn’t care about anybody. And the only people that were making any money in that Bass Choir were Richard Davis, Ron Carter and me. We were making a record date. And we was working a lot.
